Bug_Title: AssertJ methods setting the assertion context should come before an assertion
Bug_Details:
Describing, setting error message or adding a comparator in AssertJ must be done before calling the
assertion, otherwise, settings will not be taken into account.
This rule raises an issue when one of the method (with all similar methods):
as describedAs withFailMessage overridingErrorMessage usingComparator usingElementComparator extracting filteredOn
as
describedAs
withFailMessage
overridingErrorMessage
usingComparator
usingElementComparator
extracting
filteredOn
is called without calling an AssertJ assertion afterward.
Noncompliant code example
assertThat(actual).isEqualTo(expected).as("Description"); // Noncompliant
assertThat(actual).isEqualTo(expected).withFailMessage("Fail message"); // Noncompliant
assertThat(actual).isEqualTo(expected).usingComparator(new CustomComparator()); // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
assertThat(actual).as("Description").isEqualTo(expected);
assertThat(actual).withFailMessage("Fail message").isEqualTo(expected);
assertThat(actual).usingComparator(new CustomComparator()).isEqualTo(expected);

Trigger_Explanation: The 'as', 'withFailMessage' and 'usingComparator' methods were called after the assertion 'isEqualTo' without any assertion being made in between. This causes the AssertJ to lose the context settings.
Model_Explanation: The provided Java code does not contain the described bug. The AssertJ methods setting the assertion context are correctly used before the assertion. The AssertJ methods are used in the correct order, starting with the assertion context methods (as, withFailMessage, usingComparator, usingElementComparator, extracting, filteredOn) and then the assertion method (isEqualTo, isNotEqualTo, isNull, isNotNull, etc.).
